packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-11 -- unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading for this packet. I followed the brief; I measured image pixel sizes with `sips` (to tell overviews from tiles) and did nothing else beyond the rules.

== Layout survey, face A (image-001.jpg, overview) ==
Observations:
- Packet has two overviews (image-001, image-008) and 2x3 grids of tiles for each (002-007 for face A, 009-014 for face B, inferred from pixel sizes; overlap to be checked).
- image-001: a single parchment fragment, upright, on black ground; grey rectangle masks the left half of the frame. Fragment roughly 17 cm wide x 30 cm tall by the ruler.
- Large loss/tear at top centre running down to about mid-height; the fragment is nearly split into two vertical strips, joined in the middle; a split also at the bottom centre.
- Single block of text (no columns visible), long lines across the whole width, in a small, fast cursive (documentary/notarial-looking current hand), brownish ink, much faded and stained, some dark (damp/blue-grey) staining centre.
- Top line at left begins with enlarged/display letters (looks like a heading/opening in larger, more formal letters, e.g. "...In nomine d[omi]ni"?-like display) -- to be checked on the tile.
- Modern pencil note at top right: "Stams, STA, Fag 1..?" (shelfmark-like label).
- No visible rubrics, glosses or columns; some short lines near the bottom suggest the end of a text or a subscription.
Tentative interpretation: a document (charter/notarial instrument or letter) rather than a book page. Unverified.

== image-002.jpg (face A, top-left tile; covers left strip from top edge to ~line 12) ==
Observation: the opening line is in an enlarged gothic display script (textura-like); everything below is a small, rapid cursive, very faded and abraded. A vertical ruled/bounding line (or a fold) runs down the left margin. A paper/parchment repair patch lower left (y~1070-1291). I also made a blue-channel contrast crop (scratchpad p11_002_enh.jpg, region x120-1155, y420-1291); it did not improve legibility much.

002 L2 (y~490): [illegible] ...nnu(m)? [illegible] ...   [first word begins with long strokes, perhaps "Anno"/"...nnu~"? very uncertain]

002 L4 (y~650): ...ssalem? / ...ssalcom?  [illegible] ...   [first word ends "-alem"/"-aliu(m)"? uncertain]
002 L5 (y~730): ...ys?ar...p..e? [illegible] ...  
002 L6-L8 (y~800-960): [illegible] -- only isolated ascenders/descenders visible; "...d..." at L7 start; L8 begins "D..." / "Dey..?"

== image-006.jpg (face A, bottom-left tile; lower left of fragment to bottom edge; top ~2 lines overlap 004's bottom lines) ==
Observation: main-text lines continue across; at the far left (x~210-470, y~100-760) there are groups of small, darker letters in short line-starts that look different in ink tone (darker, crisper) from the faded main text -- either later additions/annotations at line-starts, or simply better-preserved line beginnings; I cannot decide. == Face A summary of what was selected/unread ==
I read every tile of face A line by line but secured almost nothing: the display-script invocation "Jn Nomine d(omi)ni Am[...]" (002 L1), the modern pencil label "Stams, STA, Frg 125" (003), and tentative isolated words (005 L9 "Capitl(um)?", 007 L5 "et firm..?", possible names 003 L10 "Herm../Bern..", 007 L12 "Conr..?"). The cursive main text is too faded at this resolution. Suggest UV / multispectral imaging or a higher-resolution capture; raking light will not help much as the ink is lost rather than obscured.

== Layout survey, face B (image-008.jpg, overview) ==
Observations:
- Same fragment, other side (outline mirrored: the large tear is now at upper left of centre). Upright.
- Left of the frame lies a printed modern desk-calendar sheet ("Bürobedarf ... & Co, Bregenz-Innsbruck-Linz", "MAI 1964", days 17-23), with tape pieces -- evidently a wrapper/support, not part of the fragment.
- At top right of the fragment, the large display letters of face A ("...Nomine d...") show through mirrored; the cursive lines also show through faintly across the whole face. So face B appears to be the back of the document, with show-through.
- Centre: a large ink numeral "23" (later hand, darker ink).
- Lower left: a short line of writing running vertically (rotated 90 deg), possibly a dorsal endorsement (to be checked on tiles).
- Top right: pencil label again ("Stams, STA, Frg 125..").
Tentative interpretation: dorse of a single-sheet document; any genuine dorsal text is limited to the "23" and the vertical note; the rest is show-through. To be checked on tiles 009-014.

== image-009.jpg (face B, top-left tile; left strip of face B = mirror of face A's right strip) ==
Observation: no writing belonging to this face is visible; only mirrored show-through of face A's cursive lines (~12 lines, y~500-1300). I mirrored and contrast-stretched a crop (scratchpad p11_009_mirror.jpg, x100-830, y450-1346): the show-through is not clearer than face A itself, so I add no readings from it. A small red fleck at x~850,y~455 (pigment speck or modern). Faint horizontal crease at y~340.
009: no dorsal text.

== image-010.jpg (face B, top-right tile) ==
Observation: modern pencil label "Stams, STA, Frg 125v" ("Frg" could be read "Fag"; final "v" clear here) -- so face B is labelled as verso; face A's label (003) should then be "125r" with the final letter faint (my 003 reading of just "125" may be incomplete). Below: mirrored show-through of the display heading of face A ("Jn Nomine dni Am..." reversed) and of the first ~12 cursive lines. No writing belonging to this face visible on this tile; dark brown smudge at left edge (x~150-210, y~610-720) is a stain, not text.
010: no dorsal text.

== image-011.jpg (face B, middle-left tile) ==
Observation: mostly mirrored show-through of face A's lines. Two things belong to this face:
(a) Large ink numeral "23" (x~800-990, y~820-1020), dark brown-black ink, later hand; clear reading "23".
(b) A short vertical note in blue-grey ink/pencil(?) at x~290-410, y~930-1450, written along the long axis (rotated 90 deg). I cropped and rotated it (scratchpad p11_011_note.jpg, x240-460, y900-1491, red channel, x2). Reading attempt, reading from top of tile downward: ..[ʒ/3]? ..tt?..h? ..er? ..   -- essentially [illegible]; letter-like forms "..h.." and a possible "M"/"A" are all I can see. Script looks later (modern?) than the document hand, but this is uncertain.
011: dorsal content = "23" + illegible vertical note.

== image-012.jpg (face B, middle-right tile; overlaps 011 at left -- the "3" of "23" visible at x~0-110, y~820-1020) ==
Observation: only mirrored show-through of face A's lines; no writing belonging to this face.
012: no dorsal text.

== Overall limitations and summary ==
- Single-sheet document (not a codex leaf, on the evidence of the layout): face A carries one block of ~30+ long lines of small, rapid cursive under a display-script invocation "Jn Nomine d(omi)ni Am[...]"; face B (labelled "125v") carries only a later ink "23" and a vertical pencil note ending "..23", plus show-through.
- Interpretation only, unverified: invocation + cursive + bottom fold are consistent with a notarial instrument or charter.
- The cursive on face A is too faded at this resolution for connected reading; I could not produce any span of ten connected legible lines. Nearly all line readings above are letter-level guesses flagged with "?". The secure items are: the display invocation (002 L1), the labels "Stams, STA, Frg 125" (003) / "Stams, STA, Frg 125v" (010) ("Frg" vs "Fag" uncertain), and the numeral "23" (011, 013).
- Suggested next step: UV fluorescence or multispectral imaging of face A; the right strip (005, 007) has the best-preserved ink and is the place to start.
- Did not stop on the image limit; all 14 images were read. Beyond the rules I only measured image sizes (sips) and made contrast/mirror/rotate crops in the scratchpad (paths given above).
